body:
Depends on [[T-111]]. Arabic is shipping in the first wave (user decision), so
RTL is in scope from the start rather than retrofitted — retrofitting is the
expensive path, and doing it while the layer is being written costs little.

## Layout mirroring — cheaper here than expected

Surveyed both clients:

- **Android** is already nearly clean. `Icons.AutoMirrored` is in use in `Nav.kt`
  and `ListScreen.kt`, and there is NO `padding(left=/right=)` anywhere. Compose
  mirrors `start`/`end` modifiers and Row/Column automatically once
  `LayoutDirection` is RTL.
- **Web** has only six physical-direction CSS uses, and four are `left: "50%"`
  centring tricks that mirror correctly as-is:
    - `components/AppShell.tsx:44`   `left: "0.5rem"`
    - `components/ItemDialog.tsx:359-360` `left: 0` / `right: 0`
    - `pages/ListPage.tsx:290,313`   `left: "50%"`  (centring — fine)
    - `pages/AdminPage.tsx:45`       `left: checked ? ... : ...`  (a toggle knob —
      genuinely direction-dependent, must mirror)

Work: set `dir` on the document root from the active locale, convert the
remaining physical properties to logical ones (`inset-inline-start`,
`margin-inline-*`), and audit for direction-implying icons added since.

## Bidi text mixing — the part that actually costs

This app interleaves user content with UI chrome everywhere: item names, category
names, store names, notes, quantities like "2 l", prices. An Arabic UI containing
Latin item names (and vice versa) reorders confusingly without isolation.

- Web: `dir="auto"` on every element rendering user-authored text, and wrap
  interpolated user values in Unicode isolates (FSI U+2068 / PDI U+2069).
- Android: `BidiFormatter.unicodeWrap` (or the Compose equivalent) on the same
  values.

Candidates: item name, category name, store names, note, list name, list notes,
invited email, device_label, and the account initials badge.

This is invisible until someone reads the app in Arabic, so it needs an explicit
pass rather than being left to fall out of translation.

## Numerals

Arabic locales may render Eastern Arabic numerals. Prices are the risk: the wire
format is an ASCII decimal string. See [[T-125]] — the server currently ACCEPTS
non-ASCII digits while both clients reject them. T-125 closes the server door;
this ticket must additionally ensure the Arabic UI never *produces* non-ASCII
digits into a price field, and that any locale-aware number formatting used for
display is not fed back into a wire value.

## Verification

- A screenshot/manual pass of every screen under `ar`, not just unit tests.
- An automated check that no element renders user content without `dir="auto"` /
  `unicodeWrap` would be ideal but is probably not worth the machinery; a
  checklist against the candidate list above is the realistic bar.
- The AdminPage toggle knob specifically — it is the one control whose visual
  meaning inverts if it fails to mirror.
title: RTL + bidi support so Arabic ships in the first wave
